title.zh: 卷一百四十二 列傳第二十九: 答失八都魯 慶童 也速 徹里帖木兒 納麟
title.en: Volume 142 Biographies 29: Dashibadoulu, Qingtong, Yesu, Chelitiemuer, Nalin
title.raw: 卷一百四十二 列傳第二十九: 答失八都魯 慶童 也速 徹里帖木兒 納麟 Volume 142 Biographies 29: Dashibadoulu, Qingtong, Yesu, Chelitiemuer, Nalin

sentences.zh: 答失八都鲁

translations.literal: Dashibadoulu
translations.idiomatic: Dashibadoulu

sentences.zh: 答失八都鲁，曾祖纽璘、祖也速答兒，有传。

translations.literal: Dashibadoulu — his great-grandfather was Niulian and his grandfather Yesudaer; each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Dashibadoulu's great-grandfather Niulian and grandfather Yesudaer are each treated in their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 答失八都鲁，南加台子也。

translations.literal: Dashibadoulu was a son of Nanjiatai.
translations.idiomatic: Dashibadoulu was the son of Nanjiatai.

sentences.zh: 以世袭万户镇守罗罗宣尉司。

translations.literal: By hereditary succession as myriarch he garrisoned the Luoluo Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the post of myriarch and was stationed to guard the Luoluo Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 土人作乱，答失八都鲁捕获有功，四川省举充船桥万户。

translations.literal: When the native people rebelled, Dashibadoulu captured them with merit; Sichuan province recommended him to fill the post of Ship Bridge Myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: When local tribes rose in revolt, Dashibadoulu distinguished himself in capturing the ringleaders, and the Sichuan authorities recommended him for the post of Ship Bridge Myriarch.

sentences.zh: 出征雲南，升大理宣慰司都元帅。

translations.literal: On campaign in Yunnan, he was promoted to Grand Marshal of the Dali Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After campaigning in Yunnan, he was promoted to Grand Marshal of the Dali Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，特除四川行省参知政事，拨本部探马赤军三千，从平章咬住讨贼于荆襄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng he was specially appointed Vice Councilor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, given three thousand temür-chi troops of his command, and followed Grand Councilor Yaozhu to suppress rebels in Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 11 he received a special appointment as Vice Councilor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, was allotted three thousand temür-chi from his own command, and marched with Grand Councilor Yaozhu to suppress rebels in the Jing-Xiang region.

sentences.zh: 九月，次安平站。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he halted at Anping Station.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month his army encamped at Anping Station.

sentences.zh: 时咬住兵既平江陵，答失八都鲁请自攻襄阳。

translations.literal: At that time Yaozhu's army had already pacified Jiangling; Dashibadoulu requested to attack Xiangyang himself.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yaozhu's forces had already pacified Jiangling, and Dashibadoulu asked leave to take Xiangyang on his own.

sentences.zh: 十二年，进次荆门。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he advanced and halted at Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he advanced and made camp at Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 时贼十万，官军止三千餘，遂用宋廷杰计，招募襄阳官吏及土豪避兵者，得义丁二万，编排部伍，申其约束。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels numbered a hundred thousand while government troops were only a little over three thousand; he then adopted Song Tingjie's plan, recruiting Xiangyang officials and local magnates who had fled the fighting, obtaining twenty thousand volunteer militia, organizing them into units, and imposing discipline upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then numbered a hundred thousand, while government forces stood at barely three thousand. He adopted Song Tingjie's plan, recruiting Xiangyang officials and local magnates who had fled the fighting until he had twenty thousand volunteer militia, whom he organized into units and brought under strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 行至蛮河，贼守要害，兵不得渡，即令屈万户率奇兵由间道出其后，首尾夹攻，贼大败。

translations.literal: When they reached Man River the rebels held the strategic points and the army could not cross; he immediately ordered Myriarch Qu to lead picked troops by a hidden route to their rear, attacking front and rear together, and the rebels were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Man River the rebels held the strategic crossings and blocked the army's passage. He sent Myriarch Qu with picked troops by a hidden route to strike their rear while the main force attacked from the front; caught between two fires, the rebels suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 追至襄阳城南，大战，生擒其伪将三十人，腰斩之。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the south of Xiangyang city, they fought a great battle, captured alive thirty of their rebel generals, and cut them in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to the south gate of Xiangyang, they fought a major battle, took thirty rebel generals alive, and executed them by cutting them in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 贼自是闭门不复出。

translations.literal: From then on the rebels closed the gates and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the rebels shut the gates and refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 答失八都鲁乃相视形势，内列八翼，包络襄城；

translations.literal: Dashibadoulu then surveyed the terrain: within he arrayed eight wings encircling Xiangyang city;
translations.idiomatic: Dashibadoulu then surveyed the terrain and deployed eight wings within to encircle Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 外置八营，军岘山、楚山，以截其援；

translations.literal: outside he set eight camps, stationing troops on Xian Mountain and Chu Mountain to cut off their reinforcements;
translations.idiomatic: outside he established eight camps on Xian and Chu mountains to sever their lines of relief;

sentences.zh: 自以中军四千据虎头山，以瞰城中。

translations.literal: he himself with four thousand central troops occupied Tiger Head Mountain to overlook the city.
translations.idiomatic: and he personally held Tiger Head Mountain with four thousand men of the central army to command a view over the city.

sentences.zh: 署从征人李复为南漳县尹，黎可举为宜城县尹，拊循其民，以赋军馈。

translations.literal: He appointed the campaign follower Li Fu as magistrate of Nanzhang County and Li Keju as magistrate of Yicheng County, comforting and guiding the people to supply provisions for the army.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Li Fu, who had joined the campaign, magistrate of Nanzhang and Li Keju magistrate of Yicheng, charged them with reassuring the populace, and levied supplies to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 城中之民受围日久，夜半，二人缒城叩营门，具告虚实，愿为内应。

translations.literal: The people in the city, long besieged, at midnight two men let themselves down from the wall and knocked at the camp gate, reporting the full situation and offering to act as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople, worn down by a long siege, sent two men over the wall at midnight to knock at the camp gate, report the city's true condition, and offer to serve as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 答失八都鲁与之定约，以五月朔日四更攻城，授之密号而去。

translations.literal: Dashibadoulu made a pact with them to assault the city at the fourth watch on the first day of the fifth month, gave them a secret signal, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Dashibadoulu struck a pact with them to storm the city at the fourth watch on the first day of the fifth month, gave them a secret recognition signal, and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 至期，民垂绳以引官军，先登者近千人。

translations.literal: When the day came, the people lowered ropes to draw up government troops; those who first climbed numbered nearly a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointed day came, townspeople lowered ropes to haul government troops up the wall; nearly a thousand men gained the ramparts first.

sentences.zh: 时贼船百餘艘在城北，阴募善水者凿其底。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels had more than a hundred boats north of the city; he secretly recruited skilled swimmers to bore holes in their bottoms.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred rebel boats lay north of the city; he secretly recruited skilled swimmers to scuttle them from below.

sentences.zh: 天将明，城破，贼巷战不胜，走就船，船坏，皆溺水死。

translations.literal: As dawn approached the city fell; the rebels, unable to prevail in street fighting, ran for the boats; the boats were ruined and all drowned.
translations.idiomatic: As dawn broke the city fell. Unable to hold the streets, the rebels fled for the boats, but the boats had been sunk and they all drowned.

sentences.zh: 伪将王权领千骑西走，遇伏兵被擒。

translations.literal: The rebel general Wang Quan led a thousand horsemen west in flight, met ambush troops, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Wang Quan fled west with a thousand horsemen, ran into an ambush, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 襄阳遂平。

translations.literal: Xiangyang was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang was thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 加答失八都鲁资善大夫，赐上尊及黄金束带，以其弟识里木为襄阳达鲁花赤，子孛罗帖木兒为雲南行省理问。

translations.literal: Dashibadoulu was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted imperial wine and a gold belt, his younger brother Shipimu appointed darughachi of Xiangyang, and his son Boluotiemuer judicial intendant of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dashibadoulu was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and rewarded with imperial wine and a gold belt; his younger brother Shipimu was made darughachi of Xiangyang and his son Boluotiemuer judicial intendant of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 比贼再犯荆门、安陆、沔阳，答失八都鲁辄引兵败之。

translations.literal: When the rebels again attacked Jingmen, Anlu, and Mianyang, Dashibadoulu each time led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the rebels struck again at Jingmen, Anlu, or Mianyang, Dashibadoulu led his troops out and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 寻诏益兵五千，以乌撒乌蒙元帅成都不花听其调发。

translations.literal: Soon an edict added five thousand troops, with Wusa-Wumeng Marshal Chengdu Buhua placed under his command for deployment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon reinforced him with five thousand men and placed Wusa-Wumeng Marshal Chengdu Buhua under his orders for deployment.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定青山、荆门诸寨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he pacified the stockades of Qingshan, Jingmen, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he pacified the stockades at Qingshan, Jingmen, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 九月，率兵略均、房，平谷城，攻开武当山寨数十，获伪将杜将军。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he led troops against Jun and Fang, pacified Gucheng, attacked and opened several dozen stockades in the Wudang Mountains, and captured the rebel general Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he led troops through Jun and Fang, pacified Gucheng, stormed several dozen stockades in the Wudang Mountains, and captured the rebel general known as General Du.

sentences.zh: 十二月，趋攻峡州，破伪将赵明远木驴寨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he pressed the attack on Xia Prefecture and broke the mobile-tower stockade of the rebel Zhao Mingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he pressed the attack on Xia Prefecture and stormed the mobile-tower stockade held by the rebel Zhao Mingyuan.

sentences.zh: 升四川行省右丞，赐金系腰。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat and granted a gold waist-girdle.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat and granted a gold waist-girdle.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，复峡州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year he recovered Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year he recovered Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，升四川行省平章政事，兼知行枢密院事，总荆襄诸军。

translations.literal: In the third month he was promoted to Grand Councilor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, concurrently acting as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with overall command of all armies in Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he rose to Grand Councilor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, was concurrently charged with the Bureau of Military Affairs, and given overall command of all forces in the Jing-Xiang theater.

sentences.zh: 五月，命玉枢虎兒吐华代答失八都鲁守中兴、荆门，且令答失八都鲁以兵赴汝宁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Yushu Huer Tuhua was ordered to replace Dashibadoulu in guarding Zhongxing and Jingmen, and Dashibadoulu was ordered to lead troops to Runing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yushu Huer Tuhua was ordered to relieve Dashibadoulu of the garrison at Zhongxing and Jingmen, while Dashibadoulu marched with his army to Runing.

sentences.zh: 十月，诏与太不花会军讨安丰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict ordered him to join forces with Taibuhua to suppress Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict ordered him to unite with Taibuhua's army to suppress Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 是月，复苗军所据郑、钧、许三州。

translations.literal: That month he recovered the three prefectures of Zheng, Jun, and Xu held by the Miao armies.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he recovered Zheng, Jun, and Xu, which the Miao rebel armies had occupied.

sentences.zh: 十二月，复河阴、巩县。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he recovered Heyin and Gong County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he recovered Heyin and Gong County.

sentences.zh: 十五年，命答失八都鲁就管领太不花一应诸王籓将兵马，许以便宜行事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Dashibadoulu was ordered to take immediate charge of all princely and frontier generals' troops under Taibuhua, with authority to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Dashibadoulu was placed in immediate command of all princely and frontier forces attached to Taibuhua's command, with authority to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 六月，拜河南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 进次许州长葛，与刘福通野战，为其所败，将士奔溃。

translations.literal: Advancing he halted at Changge in Xu Prefecture and fought Liu Futong in the field; he was defeated by him and officers and soldiers fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Changge in Xu Prefecture and met Liu Futong in open battle, but was defeated and his troops broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 九月，至中牟，收散卒，团结屯种。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he reached Zhongmou, gathered scattered soldiers, and organized them to settle and farm.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Zhongmou, rallied his scattered troops, and organized them into farming settlements.

sentences.zh: 贼复来劫营，掠其辎重，遂与孛罗帖木兒相失。

translations.literal: The rebels again came to raid the camp and plundered the baggage train; he thus lost contact with Boluotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raided the camp again and carried off the baggage train, and he lost contact with Boluotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 刘哈剌不花进兵来援，大破贼兵，获孛罗帖木兒归之。

translations.literal: Liu Halabuhua advanced with troops to relieve him, greatly defeated the rebel army, recovered Boluotiemuer, and returned him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Halabuhua marched to his relief, routed the rebel army, recovered Boluotiemuer, and restored him to his father.

sentences.zh: 复驻汴梁东南青堽。

translations.literal: He again encamped at Qinggang southeast of Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped again at Qinggang, southeast of Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，调兵进讨，大败贼于太康，遂围亳州，伪宋主小明王遁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he mobilized troops for the advance, greatly defeated the rebels at Taikang, then besieged Bozhou; the pretender Song ruler Little Ming King fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he took the field, routed the rebels at Taikang, and besieged Bozhou until the pretender Song ruler, the Little Ming King, fled.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加金紫光禄大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp.

sentences.zh: 三月，朝廷差脱欢知院来督兵，答失八都鲁父子亲与刘福通对敌，自巳至酉，大战数合，答失八都鲁坠马，孛罗帖木兒扶令上马先还，自持弓矢连发以毙追者，夜三更步回营中。

translations.literal: In the third month the court sent Commissioner Tohuan to supervise the army; father and son Dashibadoulu personally faced Liu Futong from the si hour to the you hour, fighting several great engagements; Dashibadoulu fell from his horse, Boluotiemuer helped him mount and return first, himself holding bow and arrows and shooting in succession to kill pursuers; at the third watch of night he walked back into camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court sent Commissioner Tohuan to supervise operations. Father and son fought Liu Futong in person from mid-morning until evening in several fierce engagements. Dashibadoulu was unhorsed; Boluotiemuer helped him remount and withdraw first, then stood his ground with bow and arrow, shooting down pursuers one after another before walking back into camp at the third watch of the night.

sentences.zh: 十月，移驻陈留。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he moved his camp to Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he shifted his headquarters to Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，攻取夹河刘福通寨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he attacked and took Liu Futong's stockade at Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he stormed Liu Futong's stockade at Jiahe.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚申，次高柴店，逼太康三十里。

translations.literal: On gengshen day of the twelfth month he halted at Gaochai Inn, pressing within thirty li of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the twelfth month he encamped at Gaochai Inn, within thirty li of Taikang.

sentences.zh: 是夜二鼓，贼五百餘骑来劫，以有备亟遁。

translations.literal: That night at the second drum more than five hundred rebel horsemen came to raid; finding preparations ready they fled swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the second watch more than five hundred rebel horsemen attempted a raid, but finding the camp on alert they fled at once.

sentences.zh: 火而追之，比晓，督阵力战，自寅至巳，四门皆陷，壮士缘城入其郛，斩首数万，擒伪将军张敏、孙韩等九人，杀伪丞相王、罗二人。

translations.literal: He set fires and pursued; by dawn he urged the battle lines to fight fiercely from the yin hour to the si hour; all four gates fell; stalwarts climbed the wall into the outer city; tens of thousands of heads were cut; nine rebel generals including Zhang Min and Sun Han were captured alive; two rebel chancellors Wang and Luo were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He lit beacons and gave chase. By dawn he was driving the battle lines from early morning until mid-morning; all four gates fell, and stalwarts scaled the walls into the outer city. Tens of thousands were slain; nine rebel generals including Zhang Min and Sun Han were taken alive; and the rebel chancellors Wang and Luo were executed.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，太康悉平，遣孛罗帖木兒告捷京师。

translations.literal: On xinyou day Taikang was wholly pacified; he sent Boluotiemuer to report victory to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day Taikang was wholly pacified, and he dispatched Boluotiemuer to report the victory to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝赐劳内殿，王其先臣三世，拜河南行省左丞相，仍兼知行枢密院事，守御汴梁；

translations.literal: The emperor rewarded him with an audience in the inner hall, ennobled his forebears for three generations, appointed him Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, still concurrently directing the Bureau of Military Affairs, to guard Bianliang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him in the inner hall with words of praise, ennobled three generations of his forebears, named him Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat while retaining charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and charged him with the defense of Bianliang;

sentences.zh: 识里木雲南行省左丞；

translations.literal: Shipimu was made Left Vice Chancellor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Shipimu was made Left Vice Chancellor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒四川行省左丞；

translations.literal: Boluotiemuer was made Left Vice Chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemuer was made Left Vice Chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 将校僚属赏爵有差。

translations.literal: generals, officers, and staff were rewarded with titles in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: and his generals, officers, and staff received graded rewards of rank.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，诏朝京师，加开府仪同三司、太尉、四川行省左丞相。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year an edict summoned him to court at the capital; he was advanced to Bearer of the Golden Girdle with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, Grand Marshal, and Left Chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year he was summoned to the capital and advanced to Bearer of the Golden Girdle with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, Grand Marshal, and Left Chancellor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九月，取沟城、东明、长垣三县。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he took the three counties of Gouchang, Dongming, and Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he recovered the counties of Gouchang, Dongming, and Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 十月，诏遣知院达理麻失理来援，分兵雷泽、濮州，而达理麻失理为刘福通所杀，达达诸军皆溃。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict sent Commissioner Dalimashili to relieve him, dividing troops between Leize and Puzhou; but Dalimashili was killed by Liu Futong and all the Mongol armies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict dispatched Commissioner Dalimashili to reinforce him with troops divided between Leize and Puzhou, but Dalimashili was killed by Liu Futong and the Mongol forces collapsed.

sentences.zh: 答失八都鲁力不能支，退驻石村。

translations.literal: Dashibadoulu, unable to sustain the effort, withdrew and encamped at Shicun.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold the line, Dashibadoulu withdrew to Shicun.

sentences.zh: 朝廷颇疑其玩寇失机，使者促战相踵。

translations.literal: The court came to suspect him of toying with the rebels and missing opportunities; envoys urging battle followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: The court grew suspicious that he was indulging the rebels and missing his chances; envoys urging him to fight arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 贼觇知之，诈为答失八都鲁通和书，遗诸道路，使者果得之以进。

translations.literal: The rebels, observing this, forged letters of Dashibadoulu's collusion with the enemy and left them along the roads; envoys indeed found them and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels learned of the court's suspicions and forged letters purporting to show Dashibadoulu negotiating with the enemy, which they scattered along the roads; envoys duly found them and carried them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 答失八都鲁觉知，一夕忧愤死，十二月庚子也。

translations.literal: When Dashibadoulu learned of it, in one night he died of grief and indignation — on gengzi day of the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: When Dashibadoulu learned what had happened, he died in a single night of grief and rage — on the gengzi day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 子孛罗帖木兒别有传。

translations.literal: His son Boluotiemuer has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boluotiemuer is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 庆童，字明德，康里氏。

translations.literal: Qingtong, courtesy name Mingde, of the Kangli clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtong, courtesy name Mingde, was of the Kangli clan.

sentences.zh: 祖明里帖木兒，父斡罗思，皆封益国公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mingli Temur and father Yarousi were both enfeoffed as Dukes of Beneficent States.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mingli Temur and his father Yarousi had both been enfeoffed as Dukes of Beneficent States.

sentences.zh: 庆童早以勋臣子孙受知仁庙，给事内廷，遂长宿卫。

translations.literal: Qingtong early, as a descendant of meritorious ministers, won favor at Renzong's shrine, served in the inner court, and eventually grew up in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a descendant of meritorious ministers, Qingtong won early favor at the court of Renzong, served in the inner palace, and in time rose through the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 授大宗正府掌判，三迁为上都留守。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief judge of the Grand Imperial Clan Court, and after three promotions became Metropolitan Guardian of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief judge of the Grand Imperial Clan Court and, after three promotions, became Metropolitan Guardian of Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 又累迁为江西、河南二行省平章政事。

translations.literal: He was further promoted in succession to Grand Councilor of the Jiangxi and Henan branch secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Grand Councilor of the Jiangxi and Henan branch secretariats.

sentences.zh: 入为太府卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Director of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 复为上都留守。

translations.literal: He again became Metropolitan Guardian of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Metropolitan Guardian of Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 出为辽阳行省平章政事，以宽厚为政，辽人德之。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, governing with leniency and breadth; the Liao people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Grand Councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, where his lenient and humane rule won the gratitude of the people of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 至正十年，迁平章，行省江浙。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhizheng he was transferred as Grand Councilor administering the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 10 he was transferred to serve as Grand Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 适时承平，颇沉湎于宴乐，凡遗逸之士举校官者，辄摈斥不用，由是不为物论所与。

translations.literal: The times were then at peace, and he was quite sunk in feasting and music; whenever reclusive scholars were recommended for school offices he invariably rejected them, and for this was not supported by public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was still at peace, and he gave himself over to feasting and music. Whenever reclusive scholars were recommended for school posts, he rejected them out of hand, and for this he won little esteem among contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 明年，盗起汝、颍，已而蔓延于江浙，江东之饶、信、徽、宣、铅山、广德，浙西之常、湖、建德，所在不守。

translations.literal: The next year bandits rose in Ru and Ying, then spread through Jiang-Zhe — east of the river Rao, Xin, Hui, Xuan, Qianshan, and Guangde; west of Zhe Chang, Hu, and Jiande — everywhere defenses could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: The following year rebels rose in Ru and Ying and soon spread through Jiang-Zhe: east of the river at Rao, Xin, Hui, Xuan, Qianshan, and Guangde; west of Zhe at Chang, Hu, and Jiande — everywhere defenses collapsed.

sentences.zh: 庆童分遣僚佐往督师旅，曾不逾时，以次克复。

translations.literal: Qingtong dispatched subordinates to supervise the armies; in no more than the season's turn they were recovered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtong sent his subordinates to direct the armies, and within a season the districts were recovered one after another.

sentences.zh: 既乃令长吏按视民数，凡诖误者悉置不问，招徠流离，俾安故业，发官粟以赈之。

translations.literal: He then ordered senior officials to survey the population; all wrongly implicated were wholly left unpunished; the displaced were summoned back and enabled to resume their former livelihoods; government grain was issued to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered local officials to survey the population, cleared all who had been wrongly implicated, summoned back the displaced, restored them to their former livelihoods, and distributed government grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 省治毁于兵，则拓其故址，俾之一新。

translations.literal: The provincial seat, destroyed in war, he then expanded on its old site and made it wholly new.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial headquarters, destroyed in the fighting, he rebuilt on its old site until it was wholly renewed.

sentences.zh: 募贫民为工役而偿之以钱，杭民赖以存活者尤众。

translations.literal: He recruited poor people as laborers and paid them in cash; especially many Hangzhou people relied on this to survive.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited the poor as laborers and paid them in cash; especially many families in Hangzhou survived by this means.

sentences.zh: 十四年，脱脱以太师、右丞相统大兵南征，一切军资衣甲器仗谷粟薪藁之属，咸取具于江浙。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Toghto as Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor commanded a great army south; all military supplies — clothing, armor, weapons, grain, fodder, and the like — were wholly drawn from Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Toghto, as Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor, led a great southern campaign, and every item of military supply — clothing, armor, weapons, grain, and fodder — was levied from Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 庆童规措有方，陆运川输，千里相属，朝廷赖之。

translations.literal: Qingtong planned and arranged with method; overland transport and river carriage followed one another for a thousand li; the court relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtong organized the effort with skill: overland convoys and river barges stretched for a thousand li, and the court depended on him.

sentences.zh: 明年，盗起常之无锡，众议以重兵歼之，庆童曰：「赤子无知，迫于有司，故弄兵耳。

translations.literal: The next year bandits rose at Wuxi in Chang Prefecture; the multitude debated destroying them with heavy troops; Qingtong said: "Infants in swaddling clothes know nothing — pressed by officials, they merely take up arms.
translations.idiomatic: The following year rebels rose at Wuxi in Chang Prefecture. Many urged crushing them with heavy troops, but Qingtong said, "These are ignorant common folk driven to arms by harsh officials.

sentences.zh: 苟谕以祸福，彼无不降之理。

translations.literal: If one instructs them in fortune and calamity, there is no reason they would not submit."
translations.idiomatic: If we explain to them the consequences of fortune and ruin, there is no reason they will not submit."

sentences.zh: 」盗闻之，果投戈解甲，请为良民。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard this, they indeed cast aside weapons and armor and asked to become good citizens.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard this, they cast aside their weapons and armor and asked to return to peaceful life.

sentences.zh: 十六年，平江、湖州陷。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Pingjiang and Huzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Pingjiang and Huzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 义兵元帅方家奴以所部军屯杭城之北关，钩结同党，相煽为恶，劫掠财货，白昼杀人，民以为患。

translations.literal: Volunteer-army marshal Fang Kena stationed his troops at Hangzhou's North Pass, colluding with accomplices, inciting one another to evil, plundering goods, killing people in broad daylight — the people regarded it as a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: The volunteer-army marshal Fang Kena encamped his troops at Hangzhou's North Pass, where he colluded with accomplices, incited one another to violence, plundered goods, and killed people in broad daylight until the populace lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 庆童言于丞相达识帖睦迩曰：「我师无律，何以克敌？

translations.literal: Qingtong said to Chancellor Dashi Timur: "Our army has no discipline — how can we overcome the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Qingtong said to Chancellor Dashi Timur, "Our troops have no discipline — how can we defeat the enemy?

sentences.zh: 必斩方家奴乃可出师。

translations.literal: Fang Kena must be beheaded before troops can march out."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Kena must be executed before we can take the field."

sentences.zh: 」丞相乃与庆童入其军，数其罪，斩首以徇，民大悦。

translations.literal: The chancellor then entered the army with Qingtong, enumerated his crimes, beheaded him as a warning, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor then entered the camp with Qingtong, recited his crimes, and had him beheaded as a warning; the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 继而苗军帅杨完者以其军守杭城。

translations.literal: Soon after, Miao-army commander Yang Waner with his army guarded Hangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Miao-army commander Yang Waner garrisoned Hangzhou with his troops.

sentences.zh: 丞相达识帖睦迩既承制授完者江浙行省右丞，而完者益以功自骄，因求娶庆童女。

translations.literal: Chancellor Dashi Timur, having received imperial authorization, appointed Waner Right Vice Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; Waner grew still prouder of his merit and therefore sought to marry Qingtong's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dashi Timur, acting under imperial commission, had appointed Waner Right Vice Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; emboldened by his victories, Waner asked for Qingtong's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 庆童初不许，时苗军势甚张，达识帖睦迩方倚以为重，强为主婚，庆童不得已以女与之。

translations.literal: Qingtong at first did not consent; at that time the Miao armies were very powerful and Dashi Timur was just then relying on them as weighty; he forced the marriage arrangement, and Qingtong had no choice but to give his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtong refused at first, but the Miao armies were then at the height of their power and Dashi Timur depended on them heavily; he compelled the match, and Qingtong had no choice but to give his daughter.

sentences.zh: 明年，出镇海宁州，距杭百里，地濒海硗瘠，民甚贫。

translations.literal: The next year he went out to garrison Haining Prefecture, a hundred li from Hangzhou, the land bordering the sea, stony and barren, the people very poor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted to garrison Haining Prefecture, a hundred li from Hangzhou on a barren coast where the people were desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 居二年，盗息而民阜。

translations.literal: After two years' residence, banditry ceased and the people prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years banditry had ceased and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 至是，庆童在江浙已七年，涉历险艰，劳绩甚优著，召拜翰林学士承旨，改淮南行省平章政事，未行，仍任江浙。

translations.literal: By then Qingtong had been in Jiang-Zhe seven years, passing through dangers and hardships with very distinguished merit; he was summoned and appointed Academician Expositor-in-Chief, transferred to Grand Councilor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat — before departing he still held Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qingtong had served seven years in Jiang-Zhe through grave dangers with outstanding merit. He was summoned as Academician Expositor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Councilor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, but before he could depart he was kept at his post in Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 十八年，迁福建行省平章政事，未行，拜江南行台御史大夫，赐以御衣、上尊。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Grand Councilor of the Fujian Branch Secretariat; before departing he was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, granted imperial robes and wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Grand Councilor of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, but before he could leave he was named Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate and granted imperial robes and wine.

sentences.zh: 时南行台治绍兴，所辖诸道皆阻绝不通。

translations.literal: At that time the Southern Branch Censorate was administered from Shaoxing; all circuits under its jurisdiction were cut off and impassable.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Branch Censorate was then administered from Shaoxing, but every circuit under its jurisdiction was cut off and impassable.

sentences.zh: 绍兴之东，明、台诸郡则制于方国珍，其西杭、苏诸郡则据于张士诚。

translations.literal: East of Shaoxing, the prefectures Ming and Tai were controlled by Fang Guozhen; west of it the prefectures Hang and Su were held by Zhang Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: East of Shaoxing the prefectures of Ming and Tai were controlled by Fang Guozhen; to the west Hang and Su were held by Zhang Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 宪台纲纪不复可振，徒存空名而已。

translations.literal: The censorate's statutes and discipline could no longer be revived; it retained only an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate's authority could no longer be restored; it existed in name only.

sentences.zh: 二十年，召还朝，庆童乃由海道趋京师。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was summoned back to court; Qingtong then hastened to the capital by sea route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was recalled to court, and Qingtong made his way to the capital by sea.

sentences.zh: 拜中书平章政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄有谮其子刚僧私通宫人者，帝怒杀之。

translations.literal: Soon someone slandered his son Gangseng for privately consorting with palace women; the emperor in anger had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone accused his son Gangseng of an affair with palace women; the emperor flew into a rage and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 庆童因鞅鞅不得志，移疾家居久之，日饮酒以自遣。

translations.literal: Qingtong, discontented and unfulfilled in his ambitions, pleaded illness and remained at home a long while, drinking daily to console himself.
translations.idiomatic: Disheartened and unable to advance, Qingtong pleaded illness and stayed home for a long while, drinking every day to dull his grief.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，诏拜陕西行省左丞相。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year an edict appointed him Left Chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year an edict named him Left Chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 时李思齐拥兵关中，庆童至则御之以礼，待之以和。

translations.literal: At that time Li Sizhi held troops in Guanzhong; when Qingtong arrived he treated him with ritual propriety and dealt with him harmoniously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhi then held the Guanzhong region with his army; when Qingtong arrived he received him with full ceremony and treated him with conciliation.

sentences.zh: 居三年，关陕用宁。

translations.literal: After three years' residence, Guan and Shaanxi were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years Guan and Shaanxi were at peace.

sentences.zh: 召还京师。

translations.literal: He was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十八年七月，大明兵逼京城，帝与皇太子及六宫至于宰臣近戚皆北奔，而命淮王帖木兒不花监国，庆童为中书左丞相以辅之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year Ming troops pressed the capital; the emperor with the crown prince and the six palaces down to chief ministers and close kin all fled north; the Huai Prince Temür Buhua was ordered to oversee the state, with Qingtong as Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year Ming forces closed on the capital. The emperor, the crown prince, the inner palaces, the chief ministers, and the imperial kin all fled north. The Huai Prince Temür Buhua was left to oversee the realm, with Qingtong as Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat to assist him.

sentences.zh: 八月二日，京城破，淮王与庆童出齐化门，皆被杀。

translations.literal: On the second day of the eighth month the capital fell; the Huai Prince and Qingtong went out through Qihua Gate and were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the eighth month the capital fell. The Huai Prince and Qingtong went out through Qihua Gate and were both slain.

sentences.zh: 也速，蒙古人，倜傥有能名。

translations.literal: Yesu, a Mongol, was unconventional and bore a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu, a Mongol, was free-spirited and widely known for his abilities.

sentences.zh: 由宿卫历尚乘寺提点，迁宣政院参议。

translations.literal: From the palace guard he passed through Intendant of the Imperial Carriage Office and was transferred to Counselor of the Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the palace guard through Intendant of the Imperial Carriage Office to Counselor of the Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，河南贼芝麻李据徐州，也速从太师脱脱南征，徐州城坚不可猝拔，脱脱用也速计，以巨石为砲，昼夜攻之不息，贼困莫能支。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng the Henan rebel Sesame Li held Xuzhou; Yesu followed Grand Preceptor Toghto on the southern campaign; Xuzhou's walls were strong and could not be taken in a rush; Toghto used Yesu's plan, making stone boulders into catapults, attacking day and night without cease until the rebels, hard pressed, could not hold out.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 14 the Henan rebel Sesame Li seized Xuzhou. Yesu accompanied Grand Preceptor Toghto on the southern campaign. The city was too strong to storm at once, so Toghto adopted Yesu's plan of stone-throwing engines and attacked day and night without pause until the rebels, exhausted, could hold out no longer.

sentences.zh: 也速又攻破其南关外城，贼遂遁走。

translations.literal: Yesu again stormed the outer city at the south gate, and the rebels then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu then breached the outer city at the south gate, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 以功除同知中政院事。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Associate Director of the Central Court for Governance.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed Associate Director of the Central Court for Governance.

sentences.zh: 继又领军从父太尉月阔察兒征淮西，会贼围安丰，即往援之。

translations.literal: He then again led troops following his father Grand Marshal Yuekuachaer on campaign in Huai-west; when rebels besieged Anfeng he immediately went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: He next led troops under his father, Grand Marshal Yuekuachaer, on the Huai-west campaign. When rebels besieged Anfeng, he marched at once to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 渡淮无舟，因策马探水深浅，浮而过。

translations.literal: Crossing the Huai there were no boats; he therefore spurred his horse to probe the water's depth and floated across.
translations.idiomatic: There were no boats to cross the Huai, so he rode his horse into the river to test the depth and swam across.

sentences.zh: 贼大骇，撤围去。

translations.literal: The rebels were greatly alarmed and lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were terrified and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 进攻濠州，有诏班师，乃还。

translations.literal: He attacked Haozhou; an edict ordered withdrawal of the army, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Haozhou, but an edict ordered the army withdrawn, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 升将作院使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 复从太尉征淮东，取盱眙。

translations.literal: He again followed the Grand Marshal on campaign in Huai-east and took Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the Grand Marshal on the Huai-east campaign and captured Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 迁淮南行枢密院副使，升同知枢密院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Huainan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and then promoted to Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 讨贼海州，大败之。

translations.literal: He suppressed rebels in Haizhou and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against rebels in Haizhou and routed them.

sentences.zh: 贼走，航海袭山东，尽有其地。

translations.literal: The rebels fled, sailed by sea to strike Shandong, and wholly possessed that region.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled by sea, raided Shandong, and occupied the whole province.

sentences.zh: 也速计贼必乘胜北侵，急引兵北还，表里击之，复滕、兗二州，及费、邹、曲阜、宁阳、泗水五县，贼势遂衄。

translations.literal: Yesu calculated the rebels would surely press their victory northward; he urgently led troops back north, struck them from within and without, recovered the two prefectures Teng and Yan, and the five counties Fei, Zou, Qufu, Ningyang, and Sishui; rebel strength was thereby blunted.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu judged that the rebels would press north while their momentum held. He marched north in haste, attacked them from front and rear, recovered Teng and Yan prefectures and the counties of Fei, Zou, Qufu, Ningyang, and Sishui, and broke the rebel advance.

sentences.zh: 未几，复泰安州及平阴、肥城、莱芜、新泰四县，又平安水等五十三寨。

translations.literal: Before long he recovered Tai'an Prefecture and the four counties Pingyin, Feicheng, Laiwu, and Xintai, and also pacified fifty-three stockades including Pingshui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he recovered Tai'an Prefecture and the counties of Pingyin, Feicheng, Laiwu, and Xintai, and pacified fifty-three stockades including Pingshui.

sentences.zh: 升知枢密院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 讨蒲台贼杜黑兒，擒送京师磔之。

translations.literal: He suppressed the Putai rebel Du Heier, captured him, sent him to the capital, and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the Putai rebel Du Heier, sent him captive to the capital, and had him torn apart.

sentences.zh: 东昌贼将北寇，道出陵州，也速邀击于景州，斩获殆尽。

translations.literal: Dongchang rebels were about to raid north; their route passed Ling Prefecture; Yesu intercepted them at Jing Prefecture and killed or captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Dongchang rebels were marching north through Ling Prefecture; Yesu intercepted them at Jing Prefecture and killed or captured nearly all.

sentences.zh: 复阜城县。

translations.literal: He recovered Fucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Fucheng County.

sentences.zh: 有诏命也速以军屯单家桥，断贼北路。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yesu to station troops at Danjia Bridge to cut the rebels' northern route.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yesu to encamp at Danjia Bridge and sever the rebels' northern line of advance.

sentences.zh: 贼转攻长芦，也速往与战，流矢贯左手，不顾，转斗无前，杀贼五百餘人，夺马三千匹。

translations.literal: The rebels turned to attack Changlu; Yesu went to fight them; a stray arrow pierced his left hand — he paid no heed, wheeled and fought without retreat, killed more than five hundred rebels, and seized three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned on Changlu. Yesu met them in battle; a stray arrow pierced his left hand, but he ignored it, fought without yielding, killed more than five hundred rebels, and seized three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 于是分兵下山寨，民争来归。

translations.literal: He then divided troops to descend on mountain stockades; the people vied to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent detachments against the mountain stockades, and the people flocked to submit.

sentences.zh: 拜中书平章政事，改行省淮南。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat and transferred to administer the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat and placed in charge of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 雄州、蔚州贼继起，也速悉平之。

translations.literal: Rebels rose in succession at Xiong and Yu prefectures; Yesu pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rose in succession at Xiong and Yu; Yesu pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 知枢密院事刘哈剌不花所部卒掠怀来、云州，欲为乱，也速以轻骑击灭其首祸者，降其众隶麾下。

translations.literal: Troops under Bureau Director Liu Halabuhua plundered Huailai and Yun Prefecture and intended rebellion; Yesu with light cavalry struck down the ringleaders and accepted the rest into his command.
translations.idiomatic: Troops under Bureau Director Liu Halabuhua plundered Huailai and Yun and were plotting mutiny; Yesu rode out with light cavalry, killed the ringleaders, and enrolled the rest under his command.

sentences.zh: 贼陷大宁，诏也速往讨之。

translations.literal: Rebels took Daning; an edict ordered Yesu to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels captured Daning; an edict ordered Yesu to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 贼兵次侯家店，也速遇贼，即前与战，自昏抵曙，散而复合。

translations.literal: Rebel troops halted at Houjia Inn; Yesu met the rebels and immediately advanced to fight from dusk until dawn, dispersing and regrouping again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel army halted at Houjia Inn. Yesu met them and fought from dusk until dawn as the lines broke and re-formed again and again.

sentences.zh: 也速遣别骑绕出贼后，贼腹背受敌，大败。

translations.literal: Yesu sent separate cavalry to circle behind the rebels; caught front and rear they were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu sent a flanking force around the rebel rear; caught between two fronts, they were routed.

sentences.zh: 遂拔大宁，擒首贼汤通、周成等三十五人，磔于都市。

translations.literal: He then took Daning, captured the chief rebels Tang Tong, Zhou Cheng, and thirty-five others, and dismembered them in the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Daning, took thirty-five rebel leaders including Tang Tong and Zhou Cheng, and had them torn apart in the capital market.

sentences.zh: 召入觐，赏赉优渥，进阶金紫光禄大夫、知枢密院事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience, rewarded with generous gifts, and advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court, richly rewarded, and advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而贼雷帖木兒不花、程思忠等陷永平，诏也速出师，遂复滦州及迁安县。

translations.literal: Soon after rebels Lei Temür Buhua, Cheng Sizhong, and others took Yongping; an edict ordered Yesu to take the field, and he recovered Luan Prefecture and Qian'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward rebels Lei Temür Buhua and Cheng Sizhong seized Yongping; an edict sent Yesu to the field, and he recovered Luan Prefecture and Qian'an County.

sentences.zh: 时辽东郡县惟永平不被兵，储粟十万，刍藁山积，居民殷富。

translations.literal: At that time among Liaodong's prefectures and counties only Yongping had not suffered warfare; it stored a hundred thousand piculs of grain, fodder piled like mountains, and the inhabitants were prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Of all Liaodong only Yongping had escaped war; it held a hundred thousand piculs of grain, fodder heaped like hills, and a prosperous populace.

sentences.zh: 贼乘间窃入，增土筑城，因河为堑，坚守不可下。

translations.literal: The rebels seized the interval to slip in, added earthworks and built walls, used the river as a moat, and held firm so it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped in when they could, raised earthworks, used the river as a moat, and held the city so stubbornly that it could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 也速乃外筑大营，绝其樵采，数与贼战，获其伪帅二百餘人，平山寨数十。

translations.literal: Yesu then built a great camp outside, cut off their fuel-gathering, fought the rebels several times, captured more than two hundred of their rebel commanders, and pacified several dozen mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu built a great camp outside the walls, cut off their firewood and forage, fought them repeatedly, captured more than two hundred rebel commanders, and pacified dozens of mountain stockades.

sentences.zh: 又复昌黎、抚宁二县，擒雷帖木兒不花送京师。

translations.literal: He also recovered the two counties Changli and Funing and sent Lei Temür Buhua captive to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also recovered Changli and Funing and sent Lei Temür Buhua captive to the capital.

sentences.zh: 贼急，乃乞降于参政彻力帖木兒，为请命于朝。

translations.literal: The rebels, pressed hard, then begged to surrender to Vice Councilor Chelitiemuer, who sought orders from court on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, the rebels begged to surrender to Vice Councilor Chelitiemuer, who petitioned the court on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 诏许之，命也速退师。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it and ordered Yesu to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted their plea and ordered Yesu to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 也速度贼必以计怠我师，乃严备以侦之。

translations.literal: Yesu judged the rebels would surely use a stratagem to lull his army; he therefore kept strict readiness to watch them.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu judged that the rebels would feign submission to lull his army, and kept strict watch.

sentences.zh: 程思忠果弃城遁去，亟追至瑞州，杀获万计。

translations.literal: Cheng Sizhong indeed abandoned the city and fled; he urgently pursued to Ruizhou and killed or captured on the order of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Sizhong did abandon the city and flee; Yesu pursued swiftly to Ruizhou and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 贼遂东走金复州。

translations.literal: The rebels then fled east toward Jin-Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then fled east toward Jin-Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 诏还京师。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 拜辽阳行省左丞相，知行枢密院事，抚安迤东兵农，委以便宜，开省于永平，总兵如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, concurrently directing the Bureau of Military Affairs, to pacify soldiers and farmers in eastern Liaodong, entrusted with discretionary authority, opening the secretariat at Yongping while retaining overall military command as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Left Chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat and charged with the Bureau of Military Affairs to pacify troops and farmers in eastern Liaodong, with discretionary authority, a secretariat opened at Yongping, and overall command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 金、复、海、盖、乾、王等贼并起，西侵兴中州，阴由海道趋永平，闻也速开省乃止。

translations.literal: Rebels of Jin, Fu, Hai, Gai, Qian, Wang, and others rose together, invaded Xingzhong Prefecture from the west, and secretly by sea route pressed toward Yongping; hearing Yesu had opened the secretariat they halted.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel bands from Jin, Fu, Hai, Gai, Qian, Wang, and elsewhere rose together, invaded Xingzhong from the west, and secretly moved by sea toward Yongping, but halted when they learned Yesu had established his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 也速亟分兵防其冲突。

translations.literal: Yesu urgently divided troops to guard against their thrusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu quickly divided his forces to block their thrusts.

sentences.zh: 贼乃转攻大宁，为守将王聚所败，斩其渠魁，众溃，皆西走。

translations.literal: The rebels then turned to attack Daning, were defeated by the defending general Wang Ju, had their chieftains beheaded, the host routed, and all fled west.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then turned on Daning, were defeated by the garrison commander Wang Ju, lost their leaders, broke, and fled west.

sentences.zh: 也速虑贼窥上都，即调右丞忽林台提兵护上都，简精锐自蹑贼后。

translations.literal: Yesu feared the rebels would spy out Shangdu; he immediately transferred Right Vice Chancellor Hulin Tai to lead troops to guard Shangdu and himself selected elite troops to follow the rebels' rear.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the rebels would threaten Shangdu, Yesu sent Right Vice Chancellor Hulin Tai to guard the upper capital and himself took picked troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 贼果寇上都，忽林台击破之，贼众又大溃。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed raided Shangdu; Hulin Tai broke them, and the rebel host was again routed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did strike at Shangdu, but Hulin Tai routed them and their army collapsed again.

sentences.zh: 永平、大宁于是始平。

translations.literal: Yongping and Daning were thereby first pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping and Daning were at last pacified.

sentences.zh: 乃分命官属，劳来安辑其民，使什伍相保以事耕种，民为立石颂其勋德。

translations.literal: He then assigned officials to comfort and settle the people, made households of ten and five mutually guarantee one another for farming, and the people erected stones praising his merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officials to comfort and resettle the people, organized households into mutual-aid groups for farming, and the people set up stone monuments praising his achievements.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，孛罗帖木兒与右丞相搠思监、宦者朴不花有怨，遣兵犯阙，执二人以去，而也速遂拜中书左丞相。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Boluotiemuer had a grievance against Right Chancellor Toghua and the eunuch Punuhua; he sent troops to assault the palace, seized the two and carried them off, and Yesu was then appointed Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Boluotiemuer, at odds with Right Chancellor Toghua and the eunuch Punuhua, marched on the palace, seized both men, and carried them off; Yesu was then named Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七月，孛罗帖木兒留兵守大同，自率兵复向阙。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Boluotiemuer left troops to guard Datong and himself led an army again toward the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Boluotiemuer left troops at Datong and marched again on the capital.

sentences.zh: 京师大震，百官从帝城守，皇太子统兵迎于清河，命也速军于昌平。

translations.literal: The capital was greatly shaken; all officials followed the emperor in defending the city; the crown prince took command of troops to meet the foe at Qinghe; Yesu was ordered to encamp at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was thrown into panic. Officials joined the emperor in defending the city while the crown prince took the field at Qinghe; Yesu was ordered to encamp at Changping.

sentences.zh: 而孛罗帖木兒前锋已度居庸关，至昌平。

translations.literal: But Boluotiemuer's vanguard had already crossed Juyong Pass and reached Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemuer's vanguard had already crossed Juyong Pass and reached Changping.

sentences.zh: 也速一军皆无斗志，不战而溃。

translations.literal: Yesu's entire army lacked fighting spirit and collapsed without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu's entire army had lost all will to fight and collapsed without a battle.

sentences.zh: 皇太子驰入城，寻出奔于太原。

translations.literal: The crown prince galloped into the city, then soon fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince galloped back into the city and soon fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒遂入京城，为中书右丞相，语具《孛罗帖木兒传》。

translations.literal: Boluotiemuer then entered the capital and became Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat; the full account is in the "Biography of Boluotiemuer."
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemuer then entered the capital as Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat; the full account is given in his separate biography.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，皇太子在太原，与扩廓帖木兒谋清内难，承制调甘肃、岭北、辽阳、陕西诸省诸王兵入讨孛罗帖木兒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the crown prince was at Taiyuan and with Köke Temür plotted to clear the internal crisis; acting under commission he mobilized princely troops of Gansu, Lingbei, Liaoyang, Shaanxi, and other provinces to enter and suppress Boluotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the crown prince at Taiyuan joined Köke Temür in plotting to end the civil strife and, acting under commission, mobilized princely armies from Gansu, Lingbei, Liaoyang, Shaanxi, and other provinces against Boluotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒乃遣御史大夫秃坚帖木兒率兵攻上都附皇太子者，且以御岭北之兵，又调也速率兵南御扩廓帖木兒部将竹贞、貊高等。

translations.literal: Boluotiemuer then sent Censor-in-Chief Tujian Temür with troops to attack Shangdu, which favored the crown prince, and also to hold off Lingbei forces; he also ordered Yesu to lead troops south to resist Köke Temür's generals Zhuzhen, Mo Gao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemuer sent Censor-in-Chief Tujian Temür to attack Shangdu, which supported the crown prince, and to hold the Lingbei armies in check, while ordering Yesu south to face Köke Temür's generals Zhuzhen, Mo Gao, and others.

sentences.zh: 也速军次良乡不进，谋之于众，皆以谓孛罗帖木兒所行狂悖，图危宗社，中外同愤。

translations.literal: Yesu's army halted at Liangxiang and did not advance; he consulted the host, and all said Boluotiemuer's conduct was reckless and perverse, plotting to endanger the altars of state; court and country shared the same indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu's army halted at Liangxiang. When he consulted his officers, all agreed that Boluotiemuer's conduct was reckless and threatened the dynasty, and that court and country alike burned with indignation.

sentences.zh: 遂勒兵归永平，西连太原扩廓帖木兒，东连辽阳也先不花国王，军声大振。

translations.literal: He then led his army back to Yongping, linked west with Köke Temür at Taiyuan, linked east with Liaoyang's King Yexian Buhua, and his army's renown greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: He marched back to Yongping, allied west with Köke Temür at Taiyuan and east with King Yexian Buhua in Liaoyang, and his army's prestige rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒患之，遣其将同知枢密院事姚伯颜不花以兵往讨。

translations.literal: Boluotiemuer was troubled by this and sent his general Associate Director Yao Boyan Buhua with troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Boluotiemuer sent his general, Associate Director Yao Boyan Buhua, against him.

sentences.zh: 军过通州，白河水溢不能进，驻虹桥，筑垒以待。

translations.literal: The army passed Tong Prefecture; the Bai River overflowed and they could not advance; they encamped at Hong Bridge and built ramparts to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Tong Prefecture, but the Bai River was in flood and blocked the advance; they encamped at Hong Bridge and built fortifications to wait.

sentences.zh: 姚伯颜不花素轻也速无谋，不设备。

translations.literal: Yao Boyan Buhua had always despised Yesu as lacking strategy and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Boyan Buhua had always despised Yesu as a fool and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 也速觇知之，袭破其军，擒姚伯颜不花。

translations.literal: Yesu, observing this, raided and broke his army and captured Yao Boyan Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: Yesu learned of this, surprised the army, routed it, and captured Yao Boyan Buhua.

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒大恐，自将讨也速，至通州，大雨三日，乃还。

translations.literal: Boluotiemuer was greatly afraid and personally led troops to suppress Yesu; reaching Tong Prefecture, heavy rain fell three days, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemuer was terrified and marched out in person against Yesu, but after three days of torrential rain at Tong Prefecture he turned back.

sentences.zh: 孛罗帖木兒先以部将保安不附己，杀之，至是又失姚伯颜不花，二人皆骁将也，如失左右手，郁郁不乐。

translations.literal: Boluotiemuer had earlier killed his officer Bao'an for not siding with him; now he again lost Yao Boyan Buhua — both were fierce generals, like losing both hands, and he was depressed and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Boluotiemuer had earlier killed his officer Bao'an for refusing to follow him; now he had lost Yao Boyan Buhua as well. Both were fierce commanders, and their loss was like losing both hands; he sank into gloom.

sentences.zh: 事败，遂伏诛。

translations.literal: His cause failed and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His cause collapsed and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，诏以也速为中书右丞相，分省山东。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year an edict made Yesu Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat administering Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year an edict named Yesu Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat with charge of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，大明兵取山东。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Ming troops took Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year Ming forces seized Shandong.

sentences.zh: 闰七月，也速与部将哈剌章、田胜、周达等御于莫州，众败溃，乃尽掠莫州残民北遁。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month Yesu with his generals Halazhang, Tian Sheng, Zhou Da, and others resisted at Mo Prefecture; the host was defeated and routed; he then plundered all the surviving people of Mo Prefecture and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month Yesu with his generals Halazhang, Tian Sheng, Zhou Da, and others fought at Mo Prefecture, was routed, plundered the surviving populace of Mo, and fled north.

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒，阿鲁温氏。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer was of the Aru'un clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer was of the Aru'un clan.

sentences.zh: 祖父累立战功，为西域大族。

translations.literal: His grandfather repeatedly established military merit and was a great clan of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had won repeated military honors, and the family was a great house of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒幼沉毅有大志，早备宿卫，擢中书直省舍人，遂拜监察御史。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer in youth was deep, resolute, and of great ambition; early he served in the palace guard, was promoted to Secretariat Direct Attendant, and then appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chelitiemuer was grave, resolute, and ambitious. He entered the palace guard early, rose to Secretariat Direct Attendant, and was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 时右丞相帖木迭兒用事，生杀予夺皆出其意，道路侧目。

translations.literal: At that time Right Chancellor Temür Dieli held power; life, death, grant, and seizure all issued from his will; travelers averted their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Temür Dieli then held power, and life, death, reward, and punishment all lay in his hands; men on the road dared not meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒抗言，历诋其奸，帖木迭兒欲中伤之。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer spoke in opposition, repeatedly denouncing his wickedness; Temür Dieli wished to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer spoke out against him, denouncing his crimes one after another, and Temür Dieli sought to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 会山东水，盐课大损，除山东转运司副使。

translations.literal: It happened that Shandong suffered floods and the salt tax was greatly reduced; he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Shandong Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck Shandong and the salt levy collapsed, he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Shandong Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 甫浃月，补其亏数皆足。

translations.literal: Within a single month he made up the shortfall in full.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he had made up the entire shortfall.

sentences.zh: 转刑部尚书，京师豪右惮之，不敢犯法，而以非罪丽法者多所全脱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice; the capital's powerful families feared him and dared not break the law, while many who had been charged without real crime he largely spared and released.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Justice. The capital's powerful families feared him and kept within the law, while many who had been charged without real cause he spared and released.

sentences.zh: 天历二年，拜中书右丞，寻升中书平章政事，出为河南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli he was appointed Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, soon promoted to Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat, and sent out as Grand Councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 2 he was named Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, soon promoted to Grand Councilor, and then posted as Grand Councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 黄河清，有司以为瑞，请闻于朝。

translations.literal: The Yellow River ran clear; the authorities regarded it as an auspice and requested it be reported to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River ran clear, the local authorities took it for an omen and asked to report it to court.

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒曰：「吾知为臣忠、为子孝、天下治、百姓安为瑞，餘何益于治。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer said: "I know that loyal ministers, filial sons, an ordered realm, and a secure populace are auspices — what else benefits governance?"
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer said, "True omens are loyal ministers, filial sons, an ordered realm, and a secure people. What else serves good government?"

sentences.zh: 」岁大饥，彻里帖木兒议赈之。

translations.literal: That year there was great famine; Chelitiemuer proposed relief.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe famine, and Chelitiemuer proposed relief.

sentences.zh: 其属以为必自县上之府，府上之省，然后以闻。

translations.literal: His subordinates thought it must go from county up to prefecture, from prefecture up to province, and only then be reported.
translations.idiomatic: His staff insisted the report must go from county to prefecture, from prefecture to province, and only then to the throne.

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒慨然曰：「民饥死者已众，乃欲拘以常格耶？

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer said with indignation: "The people starving to death are already many — and you wish to bind this by ordinary rules?"
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer said indignantly, "People are already dying of hunger in great numbers, and you would still bind us to routine procedure?"

sentences.zh: 往复累月，民存无几矣。

translations.literal: Back and forth for accumulated months, few of the people would remain.
translations.idiomatic: Months of back-and-forth paperwork would leave almost no one alive.

sentences.zh: 此盖有司畏罪，将归怨于朝廷，吾不为也。

translations.literal: This is surely officials fearing guilt and wishing to shift blame onto the court — I will not do that.
translations.idiomatic: That is only officials afraid of blame who wish to shift responsibility onto the throne. I will not do it.

sentences.zh: 」大发仓廪赈之，乃请专擅之罪。

translations.literal: He greatly opened the granaries to relieve them, then requested punishment for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: He threw open the granaries on a large scale to relieve the people, then asked to be punished for acting without authorization.

sentences.zh: 文宗闻而悦之，赐龙衣、上尊。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong heard of it and was pleased, granting him dragon robes and imperial wine.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong heard of this he was pleased and granted him dragon robes and imperial wine.

sentences.zh: 至顺元年，雲南伯忽叛，以知行枢密院事总兵讨之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun, Bohe rebelled in Yunnan; acting as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs he took overall command to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1, when Bohe rebelled in Yunnan, he was placed in charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given overall command to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 治军有纪律，所过秋毫无犯。

translations.literal: He governed the army with discipline; wherever he passed not a speck of autumn down was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: He kept strict discipline in the army, and his troops did not harm so much as a blade of grass where they passed.

sentences.zh: 贼平，赏赉甚厚，悉分赐将士，师旋，囊装惟巾栉而已。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified the rewards were very generous; he wholly distributed them among officers and soldiers; when the army returned, his baggage held only towels and combs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified he received lavish rewards and distributed them all among his officers and men. When the army returned, his baggage held nothing but towels and combs.

sentences.zh: 除留守上都。

translations.literal: He was appointed Metropolitan Guardian of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Metropolitan Guardian of Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 先是，上都官买商旅之货，其直不即酬给，以故商旅不得归，至有饥寒死者。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shangdu officials had bought merchants' goods but did not promptly pay the price, so merchants could not return home, and some even died of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, officials at Shangdu had bought goods from traveling merchants without paying promptly, so the merchants could not return home and some even died of hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒为之请。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer petitioned on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer petitioned on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 有旨，出钞四百万贯偿之。

translations.literal: An imperial order issued four million guan in paper money to compensate them.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order issued four million guan in paper money in compensation.

sentences.zh: 迁江浙行省平章政事，以严厉为政，部内肃然。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, governing with severity; within his jurisdiction all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, where his stern rule brought the whole jurisdiction to order.

sentences.zh: 寻召拜御史中丞，朝廷惮之，风纪大振。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief; the court feared him and standards of conduct were greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Censor-in-Chief. The court stood in awe of him, and official discipline was sharply restored.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，拜中书平章政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 首议罢科举，又欲损太庙四祭为一祭。

translations.literal: He was first to propose abolishing the civil service examinations, and also wished to reduce the four ancestral temple sacrifices to one.
translations.idiomatic: He led the move to abolish the civil service examinations and also proposed reducing the four ancestral temple sacrifices to one.

sentences.zh: 监察御史吕思诚等列其罪状劾之，帝不允，诏彻里帖木兒仍出署事。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Lü Sicheng and others listed his crimes and impeached him; the emperor did not consent and ordered Chelitiemuer to continue attending to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Lü Sicheng and others impeached him on a list of charges, but the emperor refused and ordered Chelitiemuer to continue in office.

sentences.zh: 时罢科举诏已书而未用宝，参政许有壬入争之。

translations.literal: At that time the edict abolishing the examinations had been written but not yet sealed; Vice Councilor Xu Youren entered to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict abolishing the examinations had been drafted but not yet sealed when Vice Councilor Xu Youren came in to argue against it.

sentences.zh: 太师伯颜怒曰：「汝风台臣言彻里帖木兒邪？

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Bayan said angrily: "Are you, a censorial official, speaking for Chelitiemuer?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Bayan said angrily, "Are you, a censorial official, speaking for Chelitiemuer?"

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「太师以彻里帖木兒宣力之故，擢置中书。

translations.literal: Youren said: "The Grand Preceptor, because Chelitiemuer proclaimed his merit, promoted him to the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "Your Lordship promoted Chelitiemuer to the Central Secretariat because he proclaimed his own merit.

sentences.zh: 御史三十人不畏太师而听有壬，岂有壬权重于太师耶？

translations.literal: Thirty censors do not fear the Grand Preceptor yet obey Youren — can Youren's weight exceed the Grand Preceptor's?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet thirty censors defy Your Lordship and heed me — can my authority possibly outweigh yours?"

sentences.zh: 」伯颜意解。

translations.literal: Bayan's mind was eased.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan's anger cooled.

sentences.zh: 有壬乃曰：「科举若罢，天下人才觖望。

translations.literal: Youren then said: "If the examinations are abolished, talent throughout the realm will be disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Youren then said, "If the examinations are abolished, men of talent throughout the realm will be bitterly disappointed.

sentences.zh: 」伯颜曰：「举子多以赃败，又有假蒙古、色目名者。

translations.literal: Bayan said: "Degree candidates mostly fail through bribery, and some falsely claim Mongol or semu names."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan said, "Most candidates fail through bribery, and some falsely claim Mongol or semu status."

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「科举未行之先，台中赃罚无算，岂尽出于举子？

translations.literal: Youren said: "Before the examinations were instituted, censorial bribery punishments were countless — did they all come from degree candidates?"
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "Before the examinations existed, countless bribery cases passed through the censorate — were they all the work of examination graduates?"

sentences.zh: 举子不可谓无过，较之于彼则少矣。

translations.literal: Degree candidates cannot be said to have no faults, but compared with those others they are fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Examination graduates are not without fault, but compared with the others their offenses are fewer.

sentences.zh: 」伯颜因曰：「举子中可任用者唯参政耳。

translations.literal: Bayan then said: "Among degree candidates the only one fit for employment is the Vice Councilor."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan then said, "Among examination graduates, only the Vice Councilor is fit for office."

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「若张梦臣、马伯庸、丁文苑辈皆可任大事。

translations.literal: Youren said: "Men like Zhang Mengchen, Ma Boyong, and Ding Wenyuan can all undertake great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "Men like Zhang Mengchen, Ma Boyong, and Ding Wenyuan are all capable of great responsibilities."

sentences.zh: 又如欧阳元功之文章，岂易及邪？

translations.literal: And as for Ouyang Yuangong's literary works — are they easy to match?"
translations.idiomatic: And as for the writings of Ouyang Yuangong — who could easily equal them?"

sentences.zh: 」伯颜曰：「科举虽罢，士之欲求美衣美食者，皆能自向学，岂有不至大官者邪？

translations.literal: Bayan said: "Though the examinations be abolished, scholars who desire fine clothes and fine food can all study on their own — is there any who would not reach high office?"
translations.idiomatic: Bayan said, "Even without the examinations, any scholar who wants fine clothes and good food can study on his own — would he not still reach high office?"

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「所谓士者，初不以衣食为事，其事在治国平天下耳。

translations.literal: Youren said: "What is called a scholar at first does not take clothing and food as his business; his business lies in ordering the state and pacifying the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "A true scholar does not make clothing and food his concern; his concern is to order the state and bring peace to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」伯颜又曰：「今科举取人，实妨选法。

translations.literal: Bayan again said: "Today the examinations recruit men and truly obstruct the selection system."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan added, "Recruitment through the examinations today truly obstructs the regular selection system."

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「古人有言，立贤无方。

translations.literal: Youren said: "The ancients have a saying: establish the worthy without fixed method."
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "The ancients said, 'Raise the worthy by no fixed method.'"

sentences.zh: 科举取士，岂不愈于通事、知印等出身者？

translations.literal: Recruiting scholars through examinations — is it not better than men who enter office as interpreters, seal-keepers, and the like?
translations.idiomatic: Is recruitment through the examinations not better than men who enter office as interpreters, seal-keepers, and the like?

sentences.zh: 今通事等天下凡三千三百二十五名，岁餘四百五十六人。

translations.literal: Today interpreters and the like throughout the realm total three thousand three hundred twenty-five persons, with more than four hundred fifty-six added each year.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters alone number three thousand three hundred twenty-five throughout the realm, with more than four hundred fifty-six added each year.

sentences.zh: 玉典赤、太医、控鹤，皆入流品。

translations.literal: Imperial attendants, court physicians, and crane-guard units all enter the ranked grades.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial attendants, court physicians, and crane-guard units all enter the official ranks.

sentences.zh: 又路吏及任子其途非一。

translations.literal: Moreover route clerks and sons of officials have paths that are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Route clerks and sons of officials have many other paths to office besides.

sentences.zh: 今岁自四月至九月，白身补官受宣者七十二人，而科举一岁仅三十餘人。

translations.literal: This year from the fourth month to the ninth, commoners appointed to office receiving commissions numbered seventy-two, while the examinations in one year yield only a little over thirty.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month to the ninth this year, seventy-two men of no prior rank received appointments and commissions, while the examinations produce barely thirty in a year.

sentences.zh: 太师试思之，科举于选法果相妨邪？

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, consider this — do the examinations truly obstruct the selection system?"
