translations.idiomatic: Consider, Grand Preceptor — do the examinations truly obstruct the selection system?"

sentences.zh: 」伯颜心然其言，然其议已定，不可中辍，乃为温言慰解之，且谓有壬为能言。

translations.literal: Bayan inwardly approved his words, but the decision was already fixed and could not be halted midway; he therefore spoke warm words to comfort and explain, and also called Youren eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was inwardly persuaded, but the decision was already fixed and could not be reversed. He spoke to Youren in conciliatory tones and called him eloquent.

sentences.zh: 有壬闻之曰：「能言何益于事！

translations.literal: When Youren heard this he said: "What good does eloquence do for the affair!"
translations.idiomatic: When Youren heard this he said, "What good is eloquence when it changes nothing!"

sentences.zh: 」彻里帖木兒时在座，曰：「参政坐，无多言也。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer was then present and said: "Vice Councilor, sit — speak no more."
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer, who was present, said, "Vice Councilor, be seated and speak no more."

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「太师谓我风人劾平章，可共坐邪？

translations.literal: Youren said: "The Grand Preceptor says I, a censorial man, impeached the Grand Councilor — can we sit together?"
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "Your Lordship says I, a censor, impeached the Grand Councilor — can we sit together?"

sentences.zh: 」彻里帖木兒笑曰：「吾固未尝信此语也。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer laughed and said: "I never believed that talk in the first place."
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer laughed and said, "I never believed that talk in the first place."

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「宜平章之不信也，设有壬果风人言平章，则言之必中矣，岂止如此而已。

translations.literal: Youren said: "It is fitting the Grand Councilor did not believe it — if Youren truly were a censorial man speaking of the Grand Councilor, my words would surely hit the mark, not merely this much."
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "No wonder the Grand Councilor did not believe it. If I truly were a censor speaking against him, my words would have hit far harder than this."

sentences.zh: 」众皆笑而罢。

translations.literal: All laughed and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone laughed, and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 翌日，崇天门宣诏，特令有壬为班首以折辱之。

translations.literal: The next day at Chongtian Gate the edict was proclaimed, with Youren specially made lead officer to humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the edict was proclaimed at Chongtian Gate, with Youren deliberately placed at the head of the ceremony to humiliate him.

sentences.zh: 有壬惧及祸，勉从之。

translations.literal: Youren feared disaster would reach him and reluctantly complied.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisal, Youren reluctantly complied.

sentences.zh: 治书侍御史普化诮有壬曰：「参政可谓过河拆桥者矣。

translations.literal: Investigating Secretary Puhua mocked Youren, saying: "The Vice Councilor may be called one who tears down the bridge after crossing the river."
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Secretary Puhua mocked him, saying, "The Vice Councilor is one who tears down the bridge after he has crossed the river."

sentences.zh: 」有壬以为大耻，遂移疾不出。

translations.literal: Youren regarded this as a great shame and then pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Youren took this as a deep shame, pleaded illness, and refused to leave his house.

sentences.zh: 初，彻里帖木兒之在江浙也，会行科举，驿请考官，供张甚盛，心颇不平，故其入中书，以罢科举为第一事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chelitiemuer was in Jiang-Zhe, the examinations were held; post stations summoned examiners with very lavish provisions — he was quite displeased in heart; therefore on entering the Central Secretariat abolishing the examinations was his first affair.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chelitiemuer was in Jiang-Zhe, the examinations were held and the post stations lavished hospitality on the examiners — a display that rankled him. When he entered the Central Secretariat, abolishing the examinations was his first priority.

sentences.zh: 先论学校贡士庄田租可给怯薛衣粮，动当国者，以发其机，至是遂论罢之。

translations.literal: He first argued that rents from school tribute-land could supply keshig clothing and grain, moving those in power to set the mechanism in motion; by then he argued for abolition.
translations.idiomatic: He first argued that rents from school tribute-lands could supply the keshig guard with clothing and grain, moving those in power to set the plan in motion, and by then pressed for abolition.

sentences.zh: 彻里帖木兒尝指斥武宗为那壁，那壁者，犹谓之彼也。

translations.literal: Chelitiemuer once denounced Emperor Wuzong as "that one" — nabi means roughly "that fellow."
translations.idiomatic: Chelitiemuer once dismissed Emperor Wuzong as "that fellow" — nabi means, in effect, "that one over there."

sentences.zh: 又尝以妻弟阿鲁浑沙女为己女，冒请珠袍等物。

translations.literal: He also once took his wife's younger brother Aruhunsha's daughter as his own daughter and falsely requested pearl robes and other items.
translations.idiomatic: He also once passed off his wife's brother Aruhunsha's daughter as his own and falsely requested pearl robes and other imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 于是台臣复劾其罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon censorial officials again impeached him for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial officials then impeached him again.

sentences.zh: 而伯颜亦恶其忤己，欲斥之。

translations.literal: Bayan also hated his defiance of himself and wished to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan also resented his defiance and wished to remove him.

sentences.zh: 诏贬彻里帖木兒于南安，人皆快之。

translations.literal: An edict banished Chelitiemuer to Nan'an; all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banished Chelitiemuer to Nan'an, to the general satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒于贬所。

translations.literal: After a long while he died at his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 至正二十三年，监察御史野仙帖木兒等辩其罪，可依寒食国公追封王爵定谥，加功臣之号，事不行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhizheng Investigating Censor Yexian Temür and others argued his crimes could be reconsidered; he might be posthumously enfeoffed as a prince with a fixed posthumous title like the Duke of Cold Food, with a meritorious subject's designation — the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 23, Investigating Censor Yexian Temür and others argued that his case should be reconsidered and that he might be posthumously enfeoffed as a prince with a posthumous title and the designation of a meritorious subject, following the precedent of the Duke of Cold Food — but the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 纳麟，知曜之孙，睿之子也。

translations.literal: Nalin was the grandson of Zhiyao and son of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Nalin was the grandson of Zhiyao and the son of Rui.

sentences.zh: 大德六年，纳麟以名臣子，用丞相哈剌哈孙答剌罕荐，入备宿卫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dade, Nalin as son of a renowned minister, on Chancellor Hala Hasun's recommendation, entered service in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 6, as the son of a renowned minister, Nalin entered the palace guard on the recommendation of Chancellor Hala Hasun.

sentences.zh: 十年，除中书舍人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Secretariat Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Secretariat Drafting Official.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，迁宗正府郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhide he was transferred to Director of the Grand Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 4 he was transferred to Director of the Grand Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 皇庆元年，擢佥河南廉访司事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was promoted to Supervisor of the Henan Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 he was promoted to Supervisor of the Henan Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，拜监察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yanyou he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 以言事忤旨，仁宗怒叵测，中丞朵兒只力救之，乃解。

translations.literal: For remonstrance that offended the imperial will, Emperor Renzong's anger was beyond measure; Censor-in-Chief Duozhi exerted himself to save him, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorial offended the throne, Emperor Renzong's rage was immeasurable, but Censor-in-Chief Duozhi intervened on his behalf and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 又言风宪恃纠劾之权而受人赂者，宜刑而加流。

translations.literal: He also said that censorial officials who relied on impeachment power to accept bribes should be punished with penal servitude added to exile.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that censorial officials who abused their impeachment powers to accept bribes should be punished with penal servitude and exile.

sentences.zh: 四年，迁刑部员外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 六年，出为河南行省郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went out as Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was posted as Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，入为都漕运使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi he entered the capital as Commissioner of the Grand Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 3 he was recalled to the capital as Commissioner of the Grand Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 泰定中，擢湖南、湖北两道廉访使。

translations.literal: During Taiding he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Hunan and Hubei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding reign he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Hunan and Hubei circuits.

sentences.zh: 天历元年，除杭州路总管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was appointed Prefect of Hangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1 he was appointed Prefect of Hangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 锄奸去蠹，吏畏民悦。

translations.literal: He uprooted villains and removed parasites; officials feared him and the people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He uprooted corruption; officials feared him and the people were pleased.

sentences.zh: 明年，改江西廉访使。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 南昌岁饥，江西行省难于发粟。

translations.literal: Nanchang suffered famine that year; the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat found it difficult to issue grain.
translations.idiomatic: Nanchang suffered famine that year, and the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat hesitated to release grain.

sentences.zh: 纳麟曰：「朝廷如不允，我当以家赀偿之。

translations.literal: Nalin said: "If the court does not consent, I shall compensate from my family wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Nalin said, "If the court refuses, I will repay the cost from my own family wealth."

sentences.zh: 」乃出粟以赈民，全活甚众。

translations.literal: He then issued grain to relieve the people, saving very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: He then distributed grain to relieve the people and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 平章政事把失忽都贪纵不法，纳麟劾罢之。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Bashihudu was greedy, unrestrained, and lawless; Nalin impeached him and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Bashihudu was greedy and lawless; Nalin impeached him and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 至顺元年，拜湖广行省参知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was appointed Vice Councilor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 he was appointed Vice Councilor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元统初，召为刑部尚书，未至，改江南行台治书侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuantong he was summoned as Minister of Justice; before arriving he was changed to Investigating Secretary of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuantong he was summoned as Minister of Justice, but before he could take up the post he was named Investigating Secretary of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 寻升中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，召拜中书参知政事，迁同知枢密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was summoned as Vice Councilor of the Central Secretariat and transferred to Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was summoned as Vice Councilor of the Central Secretariat and then made Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 寻出为江浙行省右丞，乞致仕，不允，除浙西廉访使，力辞不赴。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Right Vice Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, begged to retire, was not permitted, was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe, and forcefully declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as Right Vice Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, asked to retire but was refused, was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe, and firmly declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，除行宣政院使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he was appointed Commissioner of the Traveling Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 2 he was appointed Commissioner of the Traveling Commission for Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上天竺耆旧僧弥戒、径山耆旧僧惠洲，恣纵犯法，纳麟皆坐以重罪。

translations.literal: The aged monk Mijie of Upper Tianzhu and the aged monk Huizhou of Jingshan indulged themselves unlawfully; Nalin punished them all with heavy crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The aged monks Mijie of Upper Tianzhu and Huizhou of Jingshan had broken the law with impunity; Nalin convicted them on serious charges.

sentences.zh: 请行宣政院设崇教所，拟行省理问官，秩四品，以治僧狱讼，从之。

translations.literal: He requested the Traveling Commission establish an Office for Honoring the Teaching, modeled on branch secretariat judicial intendants, rank fourth grade, to handle monks' lawsuits — this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that the Traveling Commission establish an Office for Honoring the Teaching, with officials of fourth rank modeled on branch secretariat judicial intendants, to handle monastic lawsuits, and the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 寻为江浙行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Soon he became Grand Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Grand Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，迁河南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Grand Councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Grand Councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，入为中书平章政事。

translations.literal: The next year he entered the capital as Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered the capital as Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，出为江南行台御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he went out as Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was posted as Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 寻召拜御史大夫，所荐用御史，必老成更事者。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief; censors he recommended for use were invariably seasoned and experienced in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Censor-in-Chief and always recommended seasoned, experienced men for censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 八年，进金紫光禄大夫，请老，不许，加太尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp, begged to retire, was not permitted, and was added Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was advanced to Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp, asked to retire but was refused, and was made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 御史劾罢之。

translations.literal: Censors impeached him and he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 退居姑苏。

translations.literal: He retired to Gusu.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to Gusu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，江淮盗起，帝命为南台御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year bandits rose in Jiang and Huai; the emperor appointed him Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when rebels rose in Jiang and Huai, the emperor appointed him Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 纳麟承诏即起。

translations.literal: Nalin received the edict and rose at once.
translations.idiomatic: Nalin accepted the edict and took up the post at once.

sentences.zh: 仍命兼太尉，设僚属，总制江浙、江西、湖广三省军马。

translations.literal: He was still ordered to hold concurrently the post of Grand Marshal, establish a staff, and take overall command of the armies of the three provinces Jiang-Zhe, Jiangxi, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named concurrent Grand Marshal, given a staff, and placed in overall command of the armies of Jiang-Zhe, Jiangxi, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 诏遣直省舍人海玉传旨尉谕之。

translations.literal: An edict sent Direct Attendant Haiyu to convey the imperial message and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent Direct Attendant Haiyu with an imperial message of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 纳麟北面再拜曰：「臣虽耄老，敢不黾勉从事，尽餘生以报陛下！

translations.literal: Nalin faced north and bowed twice, saying: "Though your servant is aged, how dare he not exert himself in service and spend his remaining life to repay Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: Nalin bowed to the north and said, "Though I am old, how dare I not exert myself to the end and spend what life remains in Your Majesty's service!"

sentences.zh: 」至则修筑集庆城郭。

translations.literal: On arrival he repaired the walls and suburbs of Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he repaired the walls and defenses of Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 会江浙杭城失守，淮南行省平章政事失列门引兵往援，次于采石。

translations.literal: It happened that Jiang-Zhe's Hangzhou city fell; Huainan Branch Secretariat Grand Councilor Shiliemen led troops to relieve it and halted at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou fell, Huainan Grand Councilor Shiliemen marched to relieve it and halted at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 纳麟使止之曰：「闻杭贼易破不足忧，今宣城危急，先宜以兵救宣城。

translations.literal: Nalin sent word to stop him, saying: "I hear the Hangzhou rebels are easy to break and not worth worry; now Xuancheng is critical — troops should first relieve Xuancheng."
translations.idiomatic: Nalin sent word to halt him, saying, "The Hangzhou rebels are said to be easy to defeat and not worth worrying over. Xuancheng is critical now — send the troops there first."

sentences.zh: 」乃调典瑞院使脱火赤率蒙古军应之，大破贼于堈下门，宣州以安。

translations.literal: He then transferred Imperial Insignia Commissioner Tuohuo Chi to lead Mongol troops to respond; they greatly defeated the rebels at Gangxia Gate and Xuan Prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Imperial Insignia Commissioner Tuohuo Chi with Mongol troops, who routed the rebels at Gangxia Gate and secured Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 已而贼陷徽州、广德、常州、宜兴、溧水、溧阳，蔓延丹阳、金坛、句容，略上元、江宁，游兵至钟山，集庆势甚危。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels took Huizhou, Guangde, Changzhou, Yixing, Lishui, and Liyang, spread through Danyang, Jintan, and Jurong, raided Shangyuan and Jiangning, and skirmishers reached Zhongshan — Jiqing's situation was very perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels seized Huizhou, Guangde, Changzhou, Yixing, Lishui, and Liyang, spread through Danyang, Jintan, and Jurong, raided Shangyuan and Jiangning, and skirmishers reached Zhongshan. Jiqing was in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 纳麟乃力疾治兵，部署士卒，命治书侍御史左答纳失理守城中，中丞伯家奴戍东郊。

translations.literal: Nalin then, straining despite illness, drilled the army and deployed the soldiers, ordering Investigating Secretary Zuodanashili to guard within the city and Censor-in-Chief Bojianu to garrison the eastern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his illness, Nalin threw himself into drilling the army and deploying the troops. He ordered Investigating Secretary Zuodanashili to hold the city and Censor-in-Chief Bojianu to garrison the eastern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 是时湖广行省平章政事也先帖木兒军和州，纳麟遣使求援。

translations.literal: At that time Huguang Branch Secretariat Grand Councilor Yexian Temür had his army at He Prefecture; Nalin sent envoys to request relief.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Grand Councilor Yexian Temür then had his army at He Prefecture, and Nalin sent envoys to request aid.

sentences.zh: 也先帖木兒曰：「我奉命镇江北，不敢往援江东。

translations.literal: Yexian Temür said: "I am ordered to guard north of the river and dare not go to relieve east of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Yexian Temür replied, "I am ordered to guard the north bank of the Yangzi and dare not march to relieve the south bank."

sentences.zh: 」纳麟复遣监察御史郑鄈力促其行。

translations.literal: Nalin again sent Investigating Censor Zheng Qin to urge his march strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: Nalin sent Investigating Censor Zheng Qin to press him again.

sentences.zh: 也先帖木兒引步骑度采石，至台城，入候纳麟疾。

translations.literal: Yexian Temür led infantry and cavalry across Caishi, reached Taicheng, and entered to inquire after Nalin's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yexian Temür led his infantry and cavalry across Caishi to Taicheng and came in person to inquire after Nalin's health.

sentences.zh: 纳麟喜，即以其故闻于朝。

translations.literal: Nalin was pleased and immediately reported the matter to court.
translations.idiomatic: Nalin was pleased and at once reported the matter to court.

sentences.zh: 已而也先帖木兒兵东趋秣陵，杀贼二千餘人，平湖熟镇，尽复上元、江宁境，乘胜入溧阳、溧水，贼溃奔广德，其据龙潭、方山者奔常州。

translations.literal: Before long Yexian Temür's army pressed east toward Moling, killed more than two thousand rebels, pacified Hushu Town, wholly recovered the territory of Shangyuan and Jiangning, pressed the victory into Liyang and Lishui; the rebels routed and fled to Guangde, while those holding Longtan and Fangshan fled to Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yexian Temür marched east toward Moling, killed more than two thousand rebels, pacified Hushu, and recovered all of Shangyuan and Jiangning. Pressing the advantage into Liyang and Lishui, he routed the rebels toward Guangde, while those holding Longtan and Fangshan fled to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 时江浙行省平章政事三旦八、右丞佛家闾亦引兵来会。

translations.literal: At that time Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat Grand Councilor Sandanba and Right Vice Chancellor Fojialu also led troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Zhe Grand Councilor Sandanba and Right Vice Chancellor Fojialu also brought their troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 所在群贼皆败北，州郡悉平。

translations.literal: Wherever the rebel bands were, all were defeated northward and prefectures and districts were wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel bands were beaten back everywhere, and the prefectures and districts were pacified.

sentences.zh: 十三年，纳麟固请谢事，从之，命太尉如故，乃退居庆元。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Nalin firmly requested to resign affairs; this was granted, he was ordered Grand Marshal as before, and he retired to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Nalin firmly asked to resign. His request was granted, he retained the title of Grand Marshal, and he retired to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 十六年九月，诏以江南行台移置绍兴，复以纳麟为御史大夫，仍太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixteenth year an edict moved the Jiangnan Branch Censorate to Shaoxing and again appointed Nalin Censor-in-Chief, still Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixteenth year an edict moved the Jiangnan Branch Censorate to Shaoxing and again named Nalin Censor-in-Chief while retaining him as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 明年，移治绍兴。

translations.literal: The next year he transferred administration to Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he moved his headquarters to Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 十八年，赴召，由海道入朝，至黑水洋，阻风而还。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he answered the summons, entered court by sea route, reached Heishui Sea, was blocked by wind, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he answered the summons and set out for court by sea, but was turned back by contrary winds at Heishui Sea.

sentences.zh: 十九年，复由海道趋直沽。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he again hastened to Zhigu by sea route.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he again took the sea route toward Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 山东俞宝率战舰断粮道，纳麟命其子安安及同舟人拒之，破其众于海口。

translations.literal: Shandong's Yu Bao led warships to cut the grain route; Nalin ordered his son An'an and those aboard the same vessel to resist them and broke their force at Haikou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bao of Shandong led warships to sever the grain route. Nalin ordered his son An'an and the men aboard his ship to resist them and defeated their force at Haikou.

sentences.zh: 八月，抵京师。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使劳以上尊，皇太子亦馈酒脯。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to comfort him with imperial wine; the crown prince also sent wine and dried meats.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to greet him with imperial wine, and the crown prince also sent wine and preserved meats.

sentences.zh: 而纳麟感疾日亟，卒于通州。

translations.literal: But Nalin's illness from exposure grew daily more urgent, and he died at Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: But the illness he had contracted grew worse day by day, and he died at Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年七十有九。

translations.literal: His years were seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-nine years old.
